record.paper_title: On some open problems of number theory
record.original_question: Is every even integer greater than 2 representable as the sum of two prime numbers?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Determine whether every even integer $n > 2$ can be written as $n = p + q$, where $p$ and $q$ are (not necessarily distinct) prime numbers. Equivalently, prove or disprove: for every integer $n \geq 4$ with $n$ even, there exist primes $p, q$ such that $p + q = n$.
artifact.status_search_result: The binary (strong) Goldbach conjecture remains a famous open problem. It has been verified computationally for all even integers up to roughly $4 \times 10^{18}$, but no general proof is known. The related ternary Goldbach conjecture was proved by Helfgott (2013).

status_evidence.title: Goldbach's conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Goldbach's conjecture is one of the oldest and best-known unsolved problems in number theory and all of mathematics.
status_evidence.claim: The binary Goldbach conjecture is still open.
